name: Crown of Aragon
alt: Kingdom of Aragon and County of Barcelona (united)

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Aragon
predecessors.text: the Kingdom of Aragon as Cliopatria draws it until 1168 (151 grid cells)

predecessors.name: County of Barcelona
predecessors.text: the County of Barcelona as Cliopatria draws it until 1168, without Cerdanya (58 grid cells)

successors.name: Kingdom of Spain
successors.text: the Crown's last Cliopatria shape (225,450 km2): the Iberian core, the Balearics, Sardinia, Sicily and Naples

ledger.x: 1162: Aragon and the County of Barcelona are united under Alfonso II.
1162: the County of Barcelona enters the union with the Kingdom of Aragon ('Aragon–Barcelona Union: 1162'); the County of Barcelona dossier ends the county in 1162 with the matching merge.
1168: the Treaty of Sangüesa gives Aragon part of the Taifa of Murcia.
1168: Cerdanya passes to Sancho, a younger member of the royal house.
1171: Alfonso II takes Teruel.
1172: Roussillon passes to Alfonso II.
1188: Cliopatria's Crown shape adds 7 cells in the Castelló and Tortosa districts, 6 of them the Almohads' in 1187.
27 May 1192: Dulce de So gives Pallars Jussà to the Crown.
1199: Peter II buys Berga.
1202: Cliopatria's Crown shape adds 2 border cells (506 km2, 1.38-1.04 W, 42.48-42.79 N) that its Navarre row held in 1201.
1206: Cliopatria's Crown shape adds 7 cells in the Castelló and Valencia districts, the Almohads' in 1205.
1209: Peter II grants Roussillon to his uncle Sancho.
31 December 1229: James I conquers Majorca.
1232: Menorca comes under James I as a Muslim tributary state.
1235: Ibiza is acquired ('Menorca (1232) and Ibiza (1235) were later acquired during the reconquest').
1236: Cliopatria's Crown shape adds the 18 cells of the County of Urgell, whose row has no shape between 1236 and 1278.
1236: Cliopatria's Crown shape adds 17 mainland cells of its Almohad row of 1235 (Castelló, Tarragona and Valencia districts).
28 September 1238: Valencia capitulates.
1241: Cliopatria's Crown shape adds 10 cells (Castelló, Tortosa and Valencia districts), 5 of them its Almohad row's in 1240 and 4 the Taifa of Valencia's.
1242: the counties of Roussillon return to the Crown.
1242: Roussillon returns to the Crown.
1242: Nuño Sanç's death returns Roussillon and Cerdanya to the Crown ('his Counties reverted to the Crown of Aragon').
26 March 1244: the Treaty of Almizra fixes the Crown's southern frontier.
26 March 1244: the Treaty of Almizra fixes the Crown's southern frontier; Cliopatria's Crown shape adds 12 cells of its Taifa of Dénia row in 1250.
1260: Cliopatria's Crown shape adds 6 cells in the Alicante province, 5 of them held by its Almohad row in 1259.
27 July 1276: James I dies and the Kingdom of Majorca is split off.
1279: the King of Majorca recognises the King of Aragon as overlord.
1282: Peter III takes Sicily.
1285: Cliopatria's Crown shape adds 7 cells on the Valencia-Alicante frontier, held by Castile in 1284, and gives back 2; the pages opened are silent.
2 November 1285: Peter III dies and the crowns divide.
1286: Alfonso III occupies Majorca.
17 January 1287: Alfonso III conquers Menorca.
1291: James II inherits Aragon and keeps Sicily.
1295: the Treaty of Anagni ends the occupation of Majorca.
1295: the Treaty of Anagni.
1305: the Treaty of Elche gives Alicante and Elche to Valencia.
1305: Cliopatria's Crown shape gives 5 cells of the Alicante province to Castile; the pages opened are silent on Murcia.
1324: James II starts to take Sardinia.
May 1343: Peter IV ends the vassalage of Majorca.
May 1343: Peter IV invades the Balearic Islands ('In May 1343, Peter IV invaded the Balearic Islands'); the Peter IV page has James's army defeated at Santa Ponça.
1344: the last of Majorca falls.
1344: the Kingdom of Majorca joins the Crown.
1353: Arborea goes to war with Aragon.
9 March 1357: Castile takes Tarazona.
18 May 1361: the peace of Terrer returns the conquests.
1363: Castile occupies Aragonese land again.
1368: Arborea nearly drives the Aragonese from Sardinia.
1375: the war with Castile ends.
1379: the Catalan duchies are the Crown's.
1379: Neopatras and the County of Salona, the rest of what 'By 1380, the Catalans were left' with, under the same overlordship; same land as catalan-company's 1379 keyframe.
1385: Cliopatria's Crown shape adds Sicily.
1388: the Acciaioli take Athens.
1390: Nerio Acciaioli takes Neopatras.
1410: Empúries escheats to the Crown.
1420: the last judicate is bought out.
1420: Aragon holds all Sardinia.
1422: Cliopatria's Crown shape adds Corsica.
10 November 1441: Alfonso V besieges Naples.
2 June 1442: Naples falls to Alfonso V ('ending on 2 June the following year'; he made 'his triumphal entrance in Naples on 26 February 1443').

2 June 1442: Alfonso V becomes King of Naples; the Crown page: 'the Kingdom of Naples was added finally in 1442 by the conquest led by Alfonso V'; he 'reunited under his dominion the kingdoms of Naples and Sicily'.
1450: Cliopatria's Crown shape drops Corsica; the Alfonso V page is silent on its end.
27 June 1458: Alfonso V dies and Naples passes to his son.
1462: France seizes Roussillon and Cerdagne.
20 January 1479: John II dies.
1487: the Crown takes Pallars Sobirà.
19 January 1493: Roussillon and Cerdagne return.
11 November 1500: the Treaty of Granada gives Ferdinand the south of Naples.
Late 1502: the partners of Granada fight.
End of 1503: the French are expelled.
End of 1503: Ferdinand holds all of Naples.
1515: Cliopatria ends the Crown's row and begins its Kingdom of Spain in 1516.

wars.name: Conquest of Majorca and Valencia by James I
wars.outcome: James I took Majorca on 31 December 1229, Menorca in 1232, Ibiza in 1235 and Valencia on 28 September 1238; the Treaty of Almizra of 26 March 1244 reserved the lands south of the Biar–Busot–Villajoyosa line for Castile.

wars.name: Battle of Muret and the loss of Occitania
wars.outcome: The page records that 'The Battle of Muret began on 12 September 1213' and that the Crown 'agreed to renounce its rights over the south of Occitania' in the Treaty of Meaux-Paris, which it dates '1229'; the James I page has the Treaty of Corbeil 'signed in…

wars.name: War of the Sicilian Vespers
wars.outcome: Peter III was crowned in Palermo in 1282; the crowns divided on 2 November 1285 and reunited in 1291; the Treaty of Anagni of 1295 forfeited Sicily to the papacy; Frederick III was crowned in March 1296; 'The war ended in 1302 in the Peace of Caltabellotta'…

wars.name: Aragonese Crusade
wars.outcome: 'Pope Martin IV declared a crusade against Aragon' and France intervened in Iberia; Roger of Lauria beat the French fleet at Les Formigues (3 September, in the 1285 campaign); Peter III died on 2 November 1285.

wars.name: Aragonese conquest of Majorca (1286)
wars.outcome: Alfonso 'invaded the realm of his uncle and conquered the island of Mallorca in 1286'; 'Some 10 years later, a new treaty - the Treaty of Anagni - ordered the return of the islands'.

wars.name: Aragonese conquest of Sardinia
wars.outcome: James II, allied with Hugh II of Arborea from 1323, took Cagliari, Gallura and Sassari in about a year; 'its de facto existence began in 1324'.

wars.name: Arborean–Aragonese wars
wars.outcome: Arborea attacked in 1353 and by 1368 left the Aragonese the port cities of Cagliari and Alghero; 'A peace treaty returned the Aragonese their previous possessions in 1388'; the Arborean army was beaten at Sanluri in 1409; in 1420 the remaining rights were…

wars.name: Conquest of the Kingdom of Majorca by Peter IV
wars.outcome: Peter IV declared James III a contumacious vassal in February 1343, invaded the Balearic Islands in May 1343, took the counties of Roussillon and Cerdanya in 1344 and brought the kingdom 'under the Crown of Aragon'; James III was 'defeated and killed at the…

wars.name: War of the Two Peters
wars.outcome: Castile took Tarazona on 9 March 1357; the peace of Terrer of 18 May 1361 returned all conquests; in 1363 Castile again occupied Tarazona and entered the Kingdom of Valencia; the peace of Morvedre of 2 July 1363 was not ratified; Peter of Castile was…

wars.name: Aragonese conquest of the Kingdom of Naples
wars.outcome: The siege of Naples ran 'from 10 November 1441 ... to 2 June the following year'; Alfonso became King of Naples on 2 June 1442 and entered the city on 26 February 1443; he 'reunited under his dominion the kingdoms of Naples and Sicily'.

wars.name: Franco-Aragonese dispute over Roussillon and Cerdagne
wars.outcome: The counties were pledged for a loan of 300,000 crowns and 'seized by France in 1462 when the loan was not repaid'; 'The Treaty of Barcelona was signed on 19 January 1493' and returned them to the Crown.

certainty.note: The Reconquista frontier with the Almohads and the taifas was a moving march; only the Pyrenean and Navarrese lines and the islands' coasts are firm.
The Almizra line (1244) fixes the southern frontier with Castile; the islands have coasts.
The Castilian occupation of 1363-1375 and the Arborean front in Sardinia have no drawn line.

Treaty lines (Barcelona 1493, Granada 1500) and coasts; soft: the Arborean front in Sardinia to 1420 (the Greek duchies are catalan-company's and Navarre is drawn by kingdom-of-navarre, neither by this dossier).
